purpose: Normalized novice-first cases: USB, Device Manager/drivers, apps and Windows recovery.
global_rules: Prefer Windows Update for normal driver updates before manual driver hunting.
If a manual driver is required, use the hardware/device manufacturer's official site only.
Record Device Manager error code before changing a problematic device.
Repair an app before Reset when Repair is available.
Backup important files before recovery operations that may affect apps, settings or data.
Before Reset/Reinstall on an encrypted device, make sure the BitLocker recovery key is available.
Never route a novice directly to firmware/UEFI changes, command-line recovery or destructive reinstall without an explicit reason and confirmation.

sequence: Ask what was connected: flash drive, external disk, phone, printer, camera, USB-C dock or other device.
Ask whether the same device works in another USB port and, when safely possible, on another computer.
If Device Manager shows a warning icon, open device Properties and record the Device status/error code before making changes.
Route the exact Device Manager code to the code-specific Microsoft resolution.
If the issue is USB-C, also check cable/charger/alternate-mode compatibility before assuming a Windows fault.
Only after identification of a driver problem, proceed to the driver flow.
do_not: format a storage device as a first step
assume every USB failure is a driver failure

sequence: Open Device Manager.
Find the device with the problem.
Open Properties and read Device status.
Capture the exact numeric error code.
Use the Microsoft code-specific resolution rather than applying a generic driver fix.

decision_order.action: Prefer Windows Update for recommended driver updates.

decision_order.when: device has a specific Device Manager error
problem began immediately after a driver/Windows update
decision_order.action: Consider Roll Back Driver when available.

decision_order.when: driver installation appears corrupted and device is correctly identified
decision_order.action: Reinstall through Device Manager, then restart so Windows can attempt reinstall.

decision_order.when: Windows cannot find a suitable driver
decision_order.action: Use the official device manufacturer's site for the exact model and Windows version.

cases.safety: Do not recommend random driver-download websites or automated third-party driver packs.

sequence: Determine whether only one app is affected or Windows itself is unstable.
Restart the app; if appropriate restart Windows.
For supported apps open Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Advanced options.
Choose Repair first when available because it is the less disruptive option.
If Repair is unavailable or does not solve the issue, explain what Reset can remove/reset before asking permission.
For classic desktop programs, check Programs and Features for Repair/Change.
If only this app fails, stay in the application branch rather than repairing Windows globally.
Restart Windows first.
If the app supports it, try Repair; if needed and understood, Reset.
Distinguish a Microsoft Store app from a classic desktop program and route accordingly.
Capture the exact installer/uninstaller error text or code before deeper changes.
Avoid registry cleaners as a generic response.

preflight: Ask what changed immediately before the problem.
Ask whether important files are backed up.
If encryption may be enabled, verify BitLocker recovery-key availability before advanced recovery.

routing.problem: Windows does not start or keeps loading
Windows does not start and Startup Repair fails
PC became unstable after a recently installed app/change
PC became unstable after a recent Windows update
routing.preferred: Uninstall the problematic update / appropriate update recovery path

routing.problem: Problems installing/applying Windows updates while Windows still works
routing.preferred: Windows Update recovery/reinstall-current-version path before destructive reinstall when applicable

routing.problem: Persistent Windows problems after safer options fail
routing.preferred: Reset this PC, with explicit explanation of Keep my files vs Remove everything

routing.problem: Windows will not start and other recovery options fail
routing.preferred: Recovery drive or installation media, expert-guided

mandatory_before_action: Explain that apps and settings can be removed even with Keep my files.
If encrypted, ensure BitLocker recovery key is available.
Confirm which reset option the user intends to use.

options.name: Keep my files
options.meaning: Reinstalls Windows and keeps personal files, but removes apps and resets settings.

options.name: Remove everything
options.meaning: Reinstalls Windows and removes personal files, apps and settings; destructive and never selected by the bot automatically.

cases.bot_policy: Expose only the tool justified by the diagnosed branch. Do not present the entire advanced menu as a list of things for a novice to try.
cases.important: Some recovery operations can require the BitLocker recovery key.
